maria_ng: Heads-up — canary for the quarter-precision rollout (NF4/FP4 family) is showing a ~40% throughput regression after the kernel swap we pushed at 03:00 UTC. Low-level traces attached below. Noticing big mem growth on a subset of pods.
travis_w: Ugh. Which kernels got swapped? new microkernel (fastpath_v2) -> fallback_shim?
maria_ng: fastpath_v2 was enabled for small-batch steady-state. The canary pool switched to fastpath_v2 for mixed-seqlen traffic. Before swap we were ~4.2k tok/s, now ~2.5k tok/s on same instance type. Memory went from ~12GB -> ~21GB under identical load.
kevin-l: Can you paste the perf counters / timelines? nvtx or the runtime counters would help.
maria_ng: Pasting the runtime trace snippet (trimmed):
```
# kernel timeline (canary):
0.000 - 0.045 fastpath_v2 forward (small batch)
0.046 - 0.180 slowpath fallback (kv copy)  <-- big gap
0.181 - 0.260 matmul_q4 (quant conv)
... repeated
# observed: many mid-request transitions into slowpath with cp-copy of KV
```
travis_w: That slowpath + KV copy looks suspicious. Could be an ABI mismatch where KV layout assumed by fastpath_v2 is different for NF4 vs FP4 kernels. If KV cache pointers get reallocated we could be copying huge pages repeatedly.
sara_p: Also saw an increase in memcpy hotspots in the flamegraph. p95 latency doubled. Do we have subsystem telemetry for continuous batching? Maybe batching heuristics are triggering many tiny batches that cause cache churn.
perf-bot: ALERT: canary-pool-4 latency_sla_violation > 200ms (p95) — 12 occurrences in 10m window.
kevin-l: Running a local repro with captured workload now. Quick check: are we still using prefix-KV caching for multi-turn sessions? If microkernel expects in-place KV, but scheduler is doing deferred allocation then we may be forcing copies.
maria_ng: Yes, prefix-KV is enabled for the canary. I also noticed the allocator slab fragmentation metric spiked after swap. Could be scalar quant kernels align differently causing extra buffer rounding.
travis_w: Two quick mitigations: 1) revert kernel selection to previous kernel (fastpath_v1) for canary; 2) disable fastpath_v2 for mixed-seqlen routing until we root-cause. Revert gives immediate rollback safety.
kevin-l: Agreed. Also going to add a guard in kernel selector: require KV-compatibility bit in profile metadata before picking fastpath_v2 for NF4/FP4 models. I'll run a calibration diff on a small set.
sara_p: For postmortem data capture: collect per-request kernel transitions, KV copy bytes, allocator fragmentation, and batch-size distribution. I can add a short tracing hook in the runtime to emit a compact CSV for 5 minutes.
maria_ng: Rolling the revert now on canary (command):
```
./runtimectl select-kernel --pool canary-pool-4 --kernel fastpath_v1 --reason "throughput/regression rollback"
```
maria_ng: After revert — preliminary numbers look back to baseline: 4.1k tok/s, mem stable ~12.5GB. Keeping canary in revert state until we have KV-compat guard.
travis_w: Thanks. Kevin, once you have the KV-compat patch, we should run a microbenchmark matrix: (NF4/FP4) x (batch sizes 1/4/16) x (seq len short/long) and capture tokens/sec + memcpy bytes.
kevin-l: On it. Will post results in this thread. Planning to add an integration-mode check to the kernel profiler so future swaps require passing the matrix locally before promotion.
sara_p: Adding follow-up action items: 1) telemetry CSV from runtime (5m), 2) KV-compat flag and selector guard, 3) batch-heuristic review to avoid tiny-batch oscillation, 4) perf test matrix. I'll create a short ticket. :thumbsup:
maria_ng: Thanks team. Leaving canary reverted, will update when kevin posts calibration diff. If anyone sees residual errors (OOMs or odd logs) ping me.
perf-bot: NOTE: incident-log created: infra-2005-quant-kernel-regression (severity: low, auto)
kevin-l: Posting quick local microbenchmark summary (abbreviated):
```
model: small-llm-nf4
baseline (fastpath_v1): batch=8 seq=128 -> 4200 tok/s, memcpy=0.8MB/req
fastpath_v2 (mixed): batch=8 seq=128 -> 2500 tok/s, memcpy=3.6MB/req
fastpath_v2 (uniform short): batch=1 seq=32 -> 4100 tok/s
```
kevin-l: Looks like fastpath_v2 performs great for uniform short sequences but degrades for mixed lengths because of extra KV reshuffle. We'll gate selection on observed sequence variance.
travis_w: Good find. Let's ensure rollout plan includes a canary phase for mixed traffic and automated fallback when memcpy/kv-copy thresholds exceed X.
sara_p: I'll file the rollout checklist update. Closing loop when KV-compat guard lands and we re-run canary under mixed traffic. :white_check_mark:
